# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## Primary Classification: Core Mechanic

---

## 1. NUMBER PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Fill cells with numbers according to constraints*

### 1.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraints
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 block
- **Hitori** — Eliminate duplicates in rows/columns by blackening cells

### 1.2 Region-Based Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbers where each number defines its block size
- **Ripple Effect** — Fill rooms with 1–N; duplicates must be separated by their value
- **Makaro** — Fill rooms with 1–N; arrows indicate which neighbor holds the maximum

### 1.3 Cross-Reference / Crossword Style
- **Nansuke** — Place multi-digit numbers from a list into a crossword-style grid

---

## 2. REGION DIVISION PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Partition the grid into regions satisfying given constraints*

### 2.1 Division into Uniform Shapes
- **Shikaku** — Divide into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** — Divide into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each)
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends

### 2.2 Division into Variable Polyominoes
- **Fillomino** — *(also listed under 1.2)* Blocks defined by the numbers within them
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per region; all colored cells connect; no 2×2 squares

### 2.3 Division into Paired / Symmetric Regions
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a matching pair of white and gray sub-regions
- **Nuritwin** — Each region contains two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connects globally

### 2.4 Division with Directional / Sequential Constraints
- **Evolomino** — Blocks grow sequentially along arrow paths, each adding one cell to the previous shape

---

## 3. CELL SHADING / PAINTING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 3.1 Connectivity and Isolation Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — White "islands" of given sizes separated by a connected black "sea"
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells; no two shaded cells touch; white cells span at most two rooms
- **Kurodoko** — Numbers count visible white cells in four directions; black cells don't touch
- **Kurotto** — Numbers in circles indicate total adjacent black cells; circles stay white

### 3.2 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Choco Banana** — Black regions must be rectangles; white regions must not be rectangles
- **Shakashaka** — Place right triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles
- **Norinori** — Shade cells in dominoes (pairs); each bold-outlined region gets exactly two shaded cells
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells in rooms; when "dropped" downward, shaded cells fill the bottom half

### 3.3 Shading with Counting Clues
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; each bold region contains exactly one wrong number clue
- **Tilepaint** — Color entire tiles; diagonal clues count black cells in row/column segments; solution depicts an object

### 3.4 Shading with Connectivity and Block Rules
- **Chained Block** — Black blocks touch only at corners (chains); each chain has uniquely shaped blocks
- **LITS** — *(also listed under 2.2)* Tetromino shading with connectivity and no-2×2 rules

---

## 4. LOOP / PATH DRAWING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Draw a single closed loop or path through the grid*

### 4.1 Unconstrained Loop with Circle/Dot Clues
- **Slitherlink** — Connect dots to form a loop; numbers indicate how many sides of each cell are used
- **Masyu** — Loop must pass straight through white circles (turning nearby) and turn at black circles (going straight beyond)
- **Mid-loop** — Loop must pass through black circles with the circle at the exact midpoint of a straight segment

### 4.2 Loop with Regional / Area Constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold region, all circles are either all straight or all turning
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each room once; alternates between visiting all moons or all suns per room
- **Suraromu** — Loop starts/ends at a numbered circle; must pass through all "Gates" in a specified order

### 4.3 Loop with Directional / Wind Constraints
- **Nagareru** — Directed loop; arrow cells define wind direction; loop cannot move against the wind and must bend with side winds
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids black cells and numbered arrow cells; arrows count black cells in their direction

### 4.4 Loop with Gate / Crossing Constraints
- **Suraromu** — *(also listed under 4.2)* Gates must each be crossed exactly once in a numbered sequence

---

## 5. CONNECTION / LINKING PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Connect elements according to given constraints*

### 5.1 Island Bridging
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with 1–2 bridges; all islands form one connected network

### 5.2 Pair Connection (Path-Based)
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching paths that fill the grid

### 5.3 Sequential / Snake Connection
- **Hebi** — Place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes don't touch; line-of-sight attack rules apply

---

## 6. MOVEMENT / PLACEMENT PUZZLES
*Primary goal: Move or place objects into valid positions*

### 6.1 Circle / Token Movement
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles into their home regions; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths don't cross
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas; gray area numbers must match the sum of entering circles

### 6.2 Light / Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs don't illuminate each other; numbered cells indicate adjacent bulb count

### 6.3 Symbol / Mark Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill cells with — or |; territory numbers indicate the difference in count; marks obey run-length limits

---

## 7. HYBRID / MULTI-MECHANIC PUZZLES
*Puzzles combining two or more primary mechanics in roughly equal measure*

### 7.1 Shading + Path
- **Nurimeizu** — Paint rooms to create walls; remaining white cells form a maze from S to G; circles lie on shortest path, triangles do not
- **Nurimisaki** — Shade cells so circled "promontory" cells each have exactly one white neighbor; white cells connect; no 2×2 blocks of either color

### 7.2 Shading + Number Placement
- **Hitori** — *(also listed under 1.1)* Shading driven by uniqueness constraints on given numbers

### 7.3 Region Division + Number Placement
- **Makaro** — *(also listed under 1.2)* Room filling with arrow-based maximum constraints
- **Ripple Effect** — *(also listed under 1.2)* Room filling with spacing constraints

### 7.4 Path + Sequential Block Growth
- **Evolomino** — *(also listed under 2.4)* Arrow-guided block sequences that grow by one cell each step
- **Pencils** — Identify pencil shapes (straight runs) and draw lines from their tips through a number of cells equal to the pencil's label

---
